title: Heavy and light gas molecules
hook: Change molecular mass and predict root-mean-square molecular speed.
misconception: root-mean-square molecular speed doubles when molecular mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v_rms = √(3kT/m) to compare root-mean-square molecular speed when molecular mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal gas at fixed absolute temperature, v_rms = √(3kT/m). When molecular mass doubles, root-mean-square molecular speed becomes 1/√2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v_rms = √(3kT/m); scaling exponent -0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal gas at fixed absolute temperature, with a nonzero initial result. If molecular mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on root-mean-square molecular speed?
recall.why: Apply v_rms = √(3kT/m) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/√3.
